ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:7, Jesus says not to use vain repetitions when praying.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Observe what Jesus says to avoid in prayer.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus cuts off the idea that many words guarantee being heard.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-01.hint: See the beginning of the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:9, tap where the Father to whom the prayer is addressed is.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Identify to whom and where the prayer is directed.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: The Father is "ours", near, and above all at the same time.

feedbackWrong.a: "Teu nome" (your name) is what is asked to be hallowed, not where the Father is.
feedbackWrong.c: "Desta forma" (in this way) introduces the prayer; it does not say where the Father is.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look for a place right after "que estás".

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.question: According to Matthew 6:7, what did the Gentiles assume when praying?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Observe the mistake Jesus corrects in prayer.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: They thought the number of words guaranteed an answer.

feedbackWrong.c: That is what Jesus says of the Father in 6:8, not what the Gentiles thought.
feedbackWrong.a: Praying in secret is Jesus' teaching (6:6), not the Gentiles' idea.
feedbackWrong.b: The verse does not speak of forgiveness; it speaks of many words.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.d: That they would be heard for speaking much
options.a: That they should pray in secret

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.question: Put Matthew 6:8 in the order of the text.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: The command, the reason and the detail: the Father knows even before we ask.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "Não vos assemelheis a eles"; "antes mesmo" closes the verse.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: The verse begins with a prohibition.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:11, for when is the bread asked?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Remember for when Jesus teaches us to ask for bread.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus teaches us to ask for this day's bread, not the month's stockpile.

feedbackWrong.c: "Sempre" (always) would ask for everything at once; the text asks for the day's bread.
feedbackWrong.a: The text does not ask for haste; it asks for this day's bread.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-05.hint: Think of the shortest time possible.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What does Matthew 6:11 say that connects to this context?
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Connect Matthew 6:11 to the life of those who lived on a daily wage.
ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: For those living on a daily wage, asking for daily bread was handing today to the Father.

feedbackWrong.c: The request is for the day's bread, not for a stockpile.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says "Dá-nos" (give us): the request includes the one praying.

ansiedade-sem-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Notice the measure of time in the request.

options.c: Securing a stockpile for the month
options.b: Praying only for other people's needs

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:8, Jesus says we must pray a lot so the Father finds out what we need.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Understand the relation between the Father's knowing and prayer.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: It is the opposite: we pray because the Father already knows, not to inform him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 6:8: the Father knows "antes mesmo de lho pedirdes" (before you ask).

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:8, tap the word that introduces the reason not to pray like the Gentiles.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in Matthew 6:8.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: It brings the reason: do not imitate the Gentiles, because the Father already knows.

feedbackWrong.a: "Antes" (before) says when the Father knows; the reason starts earlier.
feedbackWrong.b: "Não" (do not) opens the prohibition; the reason comes after.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look right after the first comma.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.question: In Matthew 6:10–11, what does the order of the requests teach about bread?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Relate the order of the requests to the place of bread.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Kingdom and will come first; bread comes after, within that care.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus tells us to ask for bread: it matters to the Father.
feedbackWrong.c: In the text, bread comes after the name, the kingdom and the will.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not tie the coming of the kingdom to surplus bread.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-03.hint: See the order: kingdom and will, then bread.

options.a: Bread is asked within the kingdom, not in its place
options.c: Bread should be asked for before everything
options.d: The kingdom only comes when there is bread to spare

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.question: In what order does the prayer go from the Father to the bread in Matthew 6:9–11?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of the prayer from the Father to the bread.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: First who God is, then his kingdom, and only then today's bread.

feedbackWrong.default: Bread comes last; the prayer begins with who God is.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: The prayer begins with the name of the one who hears.

options.b: Ask for God's kingdom to come to earth
options.c: Ask for bread just for this day

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:9, which word links the teaching of 6:8 to the prayer that follows?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Understand prayer as a consequence of the Father's care.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Prayer is a consequence: the Father knows, so pray like this, with trust.

feedbackWrong.c: "Contudo" (however) would set up a contrast; prayer follows from 6:8.
feedbackWrong.b: "Todavia" (yet) signals contrast; the text draws a conclusion.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-05.hint: It is a word of conclusion.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What links Matthew 6:11 to Exodus 16:4?
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Relate daily bread to the manna in the desert.
ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: In the desert, manna came as each day's portion; Jesus teaches us to ask the same way.

feedbackWrong.b: Manna was not for stockpiling; each day's portion came.
feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, bread is given by God, not earned.

ansiedade-cam-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Compare how often the bread arrives.

options.b: Bread stored up for the year

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.question: In Matthew 6:11, asking for bread "hoje" (today) means it is wrong to plan or save for the future.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.learningObjective: Interpret today's bread as dependence, not a ban on planning.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The request teaches daily dependence, not a ban on planning; what goes is the stockpile of fear.

feedbackWrong.true: Jesus teaches trust in the Father today; the text does not condemn prudent planning.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-01.hint: Think of what the request teaches, not what it forbids.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.question: In Matthew 6:11, tap the phrase showing that provision is asked again every morning.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that dependence is daily.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.feedbackCorrect: Provision is renewed at the pace of the day, like the manna in the desert.

feedbackWrong.c: "Nosso pão" (our bread) says what is asked, not the rhythm of asking.
feedbackWrong.b: "Dá-nos" (give us) shows it is a gift, but not the daily rhythm.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-02.hint: Look for the time expression at the end of the verse.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.question: What reading of Matthew 6:8 holds up for someone who prays anxiously?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading of Matthew 6:8 the context supports.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Whoever prays need not convince: the Father already knows the need before we ask.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus concludes the opposite: "therefore", pray like this (6:9).
feedbackWrong.d: Jesus rejects the idea of being heard for many words (6:7).
feedbackWrong.c: The text rests security on the Father who knows, not on the wording.

options.a: I can pray with few words, for the Father knows
options.b: If the Father already knows, I need not pray
options.d: The more I repeat, the more I will be heard

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.question: Which sequence reveals the thread of daily bread in the Bible?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.learningObjective: See Matthew 6:11 within the thread of bread in the Bible.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.feedbackCorrect: Daily manna prepares the request for bread, and both point to Jesus, the bread of life.

feedbackWrong.default: Start in the desert (Ex 16); the bread of life (Jn 6:35) is the goal.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-04.hint: Follow the Bible story: desert, Sermon on the Mount, John 6.

options.a: God sends manna day after day in the desert
options.b: Jesus teaches us to ask for today's bread
options.c: Jesus presents himself as the bread of life

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.question: In Matthew 6:10, what is asked to be done on earth as in heaven?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries surrender to God in prayer.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Asking God to rule also over what we cannot control takes command away from fear.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of a word; it speaks of what God wants.
feedbackWrong.c: What is asked to be done is what God wants, not a work.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.question: What links Matthew 6:8 to Isaiah 65:24?
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.learningObjective: Connect the Father who knows in Matthew to the promise of Isaiah.
ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah and Jesus say the same: God knows and answers before we finish asking.

feedbackWrong.c: Both texts say the opposite: God answers beforehand.
feedbackWrong.a: Jesus rejects many words; Isaiah says God hears while they are still speaking.

ansiedade-pro-dor-ansia-04-06.hint: Compare when God hears in both texts.

estudo:dor-ansia-04.context: Jesus teaches about prayer in the Sermon on the Mount, to people who knew long prayers meant to impress. A little later, in the same sermon, he speaks of anxiety about tomorrow (Matthew 6:34).
estudo:dor-ansia-04.focusQuestion: What would you ask God for if you prayed only for today?
estudo:dor-ansia-04.keywordGloss: The provision asked for the day; Jesus teaches us to depend on the Father today, without stockpiling tomorrow's fear.
facts: Jesus says not to use vain repetitions in prayer.
The Father knows what we need before we ask.
The prayer begins by calling God Father in heaven.
We ask that God's will be done on earth.
The bread is asked for today.
